title: RGB color generator
description:
Write a function named rgb_color_gen. It will generate rgb colors (3 values ranging from 0 to 255 each).

```py
print(rgb_color_gen())
# rgb(125,244,255) - the output should be in this form
```

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as rgb_color_gen(seed=None). When seed is provided, seed the random module with it first. Return the color as a string in the exact form 'rgb(r,g,b)' with no spaces, where r, g and b are each integers between 0 and 255 inclusive.
starter_code:
import random

def rgb_color_gen(seed=None):
    # your code here
    pass
hints: Seed random first (only if seed is not None) so results are reproducible.
Use random.randint(0, 255) three separate times to get the r, g and b values.
Build the return value with an f-string like f"rgb({r},{g},{b})" - note there are no spaces after the commas.
expected_behavior: Returns a string of the exact form 'rgb(r,g,b)' where r, g, b are integers in [0, 255]. With the same seed, the returned string is always identical.
solution:
import random

def rgb_color_gen(seed=None):
    if seed is not None:
        random.seed(seed)
    r = random.randint(0, 255)
    g = random.randint(0, 255)
    b = random.randint(0, 255)
    return f"rgb({r},{g},{b})"

hidden_tests.label: seed 0 produces the expected deterministic rgb string
seed 5 produces the expected deterministic rgb string

explanation: random.randint(0, 255) draws an inclusive random integer for each of the r, g and b channels, and an f-string assembles them into the required 'rgb(r,g,b)' text form.
